lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn  teaches the meaning form & pronunciation of comparatives
Look for understanding and address any questions or misconceptions.

“I want to write about my favourite animals! But I need your help… how can I write the words correctly? The cat is dirty but the dog is …? What about the lion? The lion is big, but the bear is…? Can you look at the box and tell me the letters I need?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - B Look and unscramble

details: Look and unscramble reinforces the ‘comparative + than’ structure by asking students to unscramble sentences comparing image pairs.
Look for confident use of the structure comparative + than and correct sequencing of sentences.”
“Thank you for helping me! I’m ready to write some sentences. Are you ready too? How quickly can you unscramble your sentences? Let’s go!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - C Look and write

details: Look and write requires students to interpret the charts and then produce a sentence using the structure ‘comparative + than’ to answer each question.
Look for correct production of sentences using ‘comparative + than’.
“You are all cleverer than me! But this activity is going to really test you - you need to write your own sentences to answer each question.”
